title: Latency hinting + geo-pin + budgeted load-shedding policy
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: As traffic grows across regions we see transient latency spikes in certain regions during peak hours and a small number of noisy customers can cause disproportionate shedding or fallback to slower cross-region replicas. We need a unified routing policy that uses client-side latency hints, geo-pinning for data locality, and capacity-aware shedding to meet region-level SLOs while minimizing cross-region traffic and expensive fallbacks.

Goal: Implement a policy that combines: 1) latency-based preference (per-request hinting + measured p50/p95 histories), 2) geo-pin rules based on account/tenant affinity, and 3) budgeted load-shedding with circuit-breaker semantics (gradual shedding tiers) so we preserve SLOs and predictable cost behavior.

This ticket covers design, implementation plan, rollout and runbook for the policy, plus required telemetry and dashboards.
design_notes:
Overview: Route selection will evaluate three independent signals in order: 1) geo-pin match (hard pin or soft preference), 2) latency preference score (derived from per-region p50/p95 + recent probe RTTs), 3) capacity headroom score (available slots / configured pool capacity). A combined score is computed via weighted sum. For requests with hard geo-pin, we only route out-of-region if local cluster is in circuit-breaker state.

Latency hinting: Clients may optionally send a latency_budget_ms header. The router treats this as a soft constraint that raises preference for lower-latency regions. If absent, router uses historical distribution for the tenant.

Capacity-aware steering: Each region publishes a capacity hint (available_concurrency_estimate) every 5s. If headroom falls below floor thresholds, circuit-breaker enters probing mode: 1) slow-path shedding (lower-priority requests decayed), 2) trial cross-region hedging for a small fraction of traffic, 3) if sustained, progressively increase shedding until SLOs stabilize.

Circuit breaker semantics: States = CLOSED, PROBING, OPEN, HALVING. Transitions triggered by region SLO breach, sustained high queueing latency, or explicit operator override. Probing windows are randomized to avoid herd behavior.

Fallback rules: When routing crosses regions, prefer region with compatible model variant and quantization profile to avoid mismatch. Apply rate caps on cross-region hops to avoid cost spikes.

Config knobs: weights for signals, latency thresholds for p50/p95, capacity floors, probe fraction, max cross-region percentage, tenant-level overrides (for VIP customers).

Telemetry: emit per-decision metrics (selected_region, score_components, reason_codes), latency budgets honored boolean, cross_region_rate, shed_reason tag.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end routing decision implemented in router service and feature-flag guarded
Latency hint header influences region selection in synthetic tests by at least 25% vs baseline
Capacity hints correctly move region into PROBING/OPEN states under load tests
No customer experiences >2x increase in 99th percentile latency when policy is enabled under canary traffic
Dashboards show selection breakdown and SLO signals for all regions
Runbook validated via chaos test (region outage) with documented fallout and mitigation steps
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: Feature-flag behind FF and default off for all tenants. Implement telemetry and dashboards. Phase 1 (Canary): Enable for internal tenants + 1% of customers in us-east and eu-west for 2 weeks; monitor p99, error rate, cross-region percent. Phase 2 (Gradual increase): 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 4 weeks with manual gates. Phase 3: Global default on with tenant opt-outs and VIP hard-pins. Emergency rollback path: disable FF or override region voting to previous simple policy.

Operator training: Ops runbook session and playbook doc published prior to Phase 1.
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for score computation and state transitions. 2) Integration tests: simulate tenant-level latency_hint header and assert region selection. 3) Load tests: ramp to 5x normal in single region and verify shedding behavior and cross-region caps. 4) Chaos test: simulated region blackout, verify failover and controlled increase in cross-region traffic within configured budget. 5) Regression test against existing canary and rollback mechanisms.

Make synthetic scenarios reproducible (k8s job manifests + load generator config) and add to CI gating for the router service.
runbook: If region p95 latency > configured SLO for 3 consecutive minutes: set region circuit-breaker to PROBING and enable trial hedging fraction 2%
If headroom < 10% for 2 minutes and errors increase > 0.5%: escalate to OPEN and start progressive shed tiers (non-VIP tenants first)
To force failover back to primary region: clear OPEN state and wait for halving window to complete or manually set CLOSED after verification
Emergency disable: flip feature flag to previous routing policy and notify on-call SREs and PM
When toggling weights or thresholds, perform a small canary and monitor routing.selection.breakdown dashboard for 15 minutes
